correctness.rationale: Uniqueness and the nontrivial rotational symmetry place the Santaló point at the origin. On a facet half-sector [0,alpha], the radial function is min(sec(theta),r); integrating its square gives the stated primal area. Independently, the support function is r cos(beta-theta) for 0<=theta<=beta (maximizer the side/arc junction), and r for beta<=theta<=alpha (the radial disk point is feasible). The polar radial function is its reciprocal, giving polar area n cos^2(beta)[tan(beta)+alpha-beta], including the endpoint geometries. Multiplying proves the formula and endpoint values. Differentiating the dimensionless product yields sin^2(beta)[(alpha-beta)(tan^2(beta)-1)-tan(beta)]. The bracket is negative for 0<beta<=pi/4; above pi/4 it is at most pi/6-1<0 using alpha<=pi/3. At the disk end the leading loss is n^2 alpha beta^3/3 with error O_n(beta^5), and beta^2=2(r-1)+O((r-1)^2). At the polygon end the chain rule gives derivative -n^2 sin^2(alpha) cos(alpha), with a quadratic remainder by analyticity. With beta=t alpha, expanding sin(beta)cos(beta) and tan(beta) through degree five gives normalized product 1-(t^3/3)alpha^2+(4t^5/15-2t^6/9)alpha^4+O(alpha^6) after dividing by pi^2. The remainders are uniform because |t|<=1. Dividing the deficit by its t=1 value gives the claimed correction and uniform O(n^-4). Independent reciprocal-support quadrature (`python3 /workspace/audit-evidence/replay.py 2`) checked 25 area pairs, with primal and polar absolute errors below 5e-9 and 1.2e-9 respectively; the universal results rest on the analytical proof.
residual_risks: Quadrature is a bounded comparison, not proof of strict monotonicity or a uniform asymptotic.
